transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-08-14 15:00 PDT
Duration: ~52m
Attendees: Lena Park (Redwood AE), Marco Reyes (Redwood SE), Priya Malhotra (AstraPay Eng Lead), Tom Brennan (AstraPay SRE), Maya Lopez (AstraPay Product)

Summary: Quick throughput snapshot focusing on continuous batching impacts and concurrency caps; discussed test results from last 24h, tuned batch window, agreed on an 8h spike run and follow-ups.

[00:00] Lena: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick check — same agenda as last week, throughput snapshot, tuning decisions, next steps. Marco, you wanna kick off with what we saw overnight?
[00:18] Marco: Yeah, thanks. so we ran the baseline with the 25ms batch window and concurrency 120. The 95th for single-token latencies stayed under the 350ms SLO but throughput plateaued around 1.2k rps for the payment-intent route. We also saw queue length spikes during the simulated morning surge.
[00:36] Priya: Right, that aligns with what we saw on our side — tail latency was okay but we lost a bunch of throughput during the 500ms+ jitter windows. Noticed some request requeues in our gateway logs.
[00:52] Tom: I also saw a few 503s when we hit the big spike; wonder if the pilot cluster hit a thread saturation on the worker side. logs were a bit noisy.
[01:10] Marco: yeah, there's a coupling between batch window and continuous batching efficiency. With 25ms we weren't packing enough tokens per batch for typical requests, so CPU/GPU utilization left money on the table.
[01:28] Maya: quick dumb question — when you say batch window, that's the time we wait to accumulate requests before dispatch, right? not queue size?
[01:35] Marco: Correct — it's the micro-window. We also have a soft queue depth that lets us flush early if we hit size thresholds.
[01:44] Lena: Thanks. So yesterday we tried 40ms and bumped concurrency cap to 140 in a canary. Marco, earliest impressions?
[01:55] Marco: The 40ms run showed a 12% throughput increase and better GPU token packing; 95p latency crept up about ~30ms but still within the 350ms target for most routes. The trade-off looks favorable for baseline daytime traffic.
[02:13] Priya: Hmm 12% is good. Did you observe any outsized tail behavior, like 99p jumps?
[02:20] Marco: The 99p did spike in a couple of mini-bursts — I think that's due to head-of-line locking when heavy requests coincide with cache misses. We saw a KV cash miss pattern (transcription: "KV cash" in logs) that magnified tail times.
[02:38] Tom: Priya and I noticed some cache invalidation storms related to our tokenization microservice. Might be contributing.
[02:46] Lena: On fallback and graceful degradation — we suggested a model variant fallback last week. Are you comfortable with automatic fallback to the smaller quantized variant if latency exceeds 600ms for 2s?
[02:59] Priya: Yes but we want to avoid quality regressions for fraud detection. We'll need threshold gating tied to the eval set.
[03:08] Marco: Agreed. we can gate fallback by an eval on a subset of requests — if top-k distributions are stable we allow fallback. We'll add telemetry tags so you can spot quality regressions quickly.
[03:26] Maya: Can you also tag the responses with the model variant used? Makes it easier in rollout dashboards.
[03:32] Marco: Yep, will include variant tags and a fallback_count metric.
[03:37] Lena: Ok, action items — Marco to push the 40ms config and concurrency bump to pilot, Priya to run the 8-hour daytime spike with realistic payment bursts.
[03:49] Priya: Quick detail — what concurrency target should we observe for the 8-hour run? 140 is the cap, but do you want us to target 120 steady with spikes to 140?
[03:59] Marco: Target 120 steady and allow bursts up to 140; that gives us headroom and stress tests the fallback.
[04:08] Tom: For the 8-hour run we'll reuse the production traffic shape but add a 20-minute spike every 2 hours to simulate peak batch loads.
[04:18] Lena: Great. Also, I ran a quick cost calc — pushing the batch window up to 40ms plus slightly higher concurrency reduces per-token cost by ~9% due to better GPU utilization, even accounting for a small latency delta. I'll share the spreadsheet.
[04:34] Maya: Are there any security implications of the telemetry tags? we need to ensure no PII is leaked in logs.
[04:40] Marco: No user PII in tags — just model variant, latency, batch size, and a hashed request-id. We'll keep the request body out of telemetry.
[04:50] Priya: About the 503s, Tom — do you think increasing the pilot cluster's worker threads would help or is the bottleneck elsewhere?
[04:58] Tom: My suspicion is the worker thread count plus the runtime's GC pauses when we hit certain request shapes. We'll collect flame graphs during the 8-hour run to confirm.
[05:10] Marco: We'll also instrument KV cache hit/miss ratios and include a metric for head-of-line wait time.
[05:18] Lena: Competition note — you mentioned evaluation versus LambdaStack in procurement. Any specific functionality there that matters?
[05:24] Priya: Mostly their autoscaling behavior and how they handle burst capacity — we want to compare latency during bursts.
[05:31] Lena: Got it. We'll include burst performance notes in the deck.
[05:36] Marco: One more technical note — if you expect many short-requests with tiny token counts, we could enable prefix caching for common prompts to reduce compute and improve tail. But that's a different engineering lift.
[05:48] Priya: That could be big for our auth flow where prompts are nearly identical. We'll discuss internally.
[05:55] Lena: Alright, let's recap and list deliverables.
[06:00] Marco: Deliverables: config diff for batch window/concurrency, telemetry additions (variant tag, fallback_count, head-of-line metric), updated runbook for fallback thresholds.
[06:10] Priya: We'll deliver the 8-hour run logs and flame graphs.
[06:14] Lena: And I'll drop cost numbers and SOC2 docs into the CRM thread.
[06:19] Maya: Sounds good. Can we do the deep-dive next Tuesday at 10am PT?
[06:23] Lena: I'll send an invite.
[06:26] Tom: One last ask — can Redwood provide a quick recommendation for queue size limits? Our current gateway default is 500 and we think that's too high for the pilot.
[06:35] Marco: We'll propose a safe default: soft queue depth 200 with a hard cap at 400 and dynamic backpressure at 75% when latency trends up. We'll put numbers and reasoning in the config diff.
[06:48] Lena: Perfect. Thanks everyone. We'll follow up in the thread.

Links shared: https://redwood.ai/pilot/astapay-telemetry (pilot telemetry folder), https://redwood.ai/docs/batching-playbook (batching playbook), CRM: CRM-48392 thread.

End of transcript.
